# Talking format

**If someone talks, in what setting and shape?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C31


## Standard yap
<a id="standard-yap"></a>

Sitting, a phone on a tripod, talking to camera.

**Looks like:** A medium shot at the desk or in the gym corner, eye contact, jump cuts and captions.

**Good at:** simplest to make; trust; volume

**Weak at:** static; relies on delivery

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals speed, trust · effort low

**How:** Tripod, Bluetooth remote, plug-in mic (not AirPods); ReCut pauses.

**Backed by:** [Yap types: standard, walking, car](../topics/filming.md#film-yap-formats), [Tripod + Bluetooth remote + plug-in mic](../topics/filming.md#film-yap-gear), [Captions on yaps for almost everybody](../topics/text.md#text-captions-on-yaps), [Frame low, leave headroom for graphics](../topics/filming.md#film-framed-graphic-headroom), [Graphic yap: one overlay every ~2 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-graphic-yap-overlay-2s) · sources L06

## Walking or car yap
<a id="walking-car-yap"></a>

Talking while moving or from the car: a FaceTime-with-a-friend feel.

**Looks like:** Handheld walking through a market, or sitting in the parked car, glancing away and back. Candid and personal.

**Good at:** authentic; natural B-roll; personality

**Weak at:** not for beginners (too many variables); audio is harder

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, story · niches travel, all · goals trust, follows · effort medium

**How:** Action mode for walking; a MagSafe mount in the car; a wired or plug-in mic.

**Backed by:** [Yap types: standard, walking, car](../topics/filming.md#film-yap-formats), [Frame low, leave headroom for graphics](../topics/filming.md#film-framed-graphic-headroom), [Yap Map: 3–5 ideas a day](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-yap-map), [Short form = awareness, long = conversion](../topics/growth.md#growth-short-awareness-long-conversion) · sources L06

## Graphic yap
<a id="graphic-yap"></a>

Talking with overlays every ~2 s: chaotic, framed with headroom, or full-screen images.

**Looks like:** As you talk, camera-roll photos, screenshots and cards cycle over or above you about every two seconds.

**Good at:** retention; shows what you say; sound-off friendly

**Weak at:** about 30 images per 60 s to gather; edit time

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, saves · effort medium

**How:** CapCut/Edits overlays; Canva for 9:16 full-screen images.

**Backed by:** [Graphic yap: one overlay every ~2 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-graphic-yap-overlay-2s), [Frame low, leave headroom for graphics](../topics/filming.md#film-framed-graphic-headroom), [Long-form talking pace 2.5–4.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-long-form-talking-pace), [Split layouts: graphic plus face](../topics/editing.md#edit-split-screen-graphic-face) · sources L06

## Podcast or conversation clip
<a id="podcast-clip"></a>

A two-person conversation, clipped into shorts or sold with a teaser.

**Looks like:** Two people in three-quarter profile with big mics; the clip opens on the most contrarian line with captions.

**Good at:** authority by association; lots of clips per session; long-form trust

**Weak at:** needs a guest and a set; clips lack context

**Best for:** formats podcast, yt-long, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals trust, reach · effort high

**How:** Two phones or a phone plus a camera; clips reframed to 9:16 with the OpenCV tracker.

**Backed by:** [Podcast body: long takes, demos as interrupts](../topics/editing.md#edit-podcast-long-takes), [Podcast set and a backdrop that teaches](../topics/filming.md#film-podcast-set), [Sell a long video with a hyper-edited teaser](../topics/editing.md#edit-teaser-hyper-edited), [Text behind your head](../topics/effects.md#l10-text-behind-head), [Cold open with later highlights](../topics/hooks.md#hook-cold-open-montage) · sources L08, L09

## Pause-and-play breakdown
<a id="pause-and-play"></a>

Talk over another reel that plays and freezes in a card, explaining each part.

**Looks like:** The source reel plays top-right, freezes and shrinks beside your head while you explain, then plays on.

**Good at:** teaching from proven examples; comments; borrowed attention

**Weak at:** originality risk; depends on someone else's work

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches tech · goals comments, saves · effort high

**How:** A rounded-card overlay plus freeze frames in CapCut or HyperFrames.

**Backed by:** [Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel](../topics/ideas.md#l10-pause-and-play-breakdown), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example), [Pause in silence to think](../topics/filming.md#film-recut-pause-method), [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook) · sources L10

## Mixing
Briar reformats the same topics across formats (green screen, whiteboard, talking head, podcast style). A standard yap becomes a graphic yap in the edit.

## Rule of thumb
Speed: standard yap. Personal and travel: walking or car. Teaching: graphic yap. Authority: podcast clip. Teardowns: pause-and-play.
